opportunity.title: Long-Term Storage and Vendor-Managed Inventory (VMI) Services for Government-Owned Microelectronics
opportunity.description: DLA Weapons Support market research for vendor-managed inventory storage, management, packaging and distribution of Government-owned serialized microcircuits: EDI ANSI X.12 transactions, Government property module and IUID registry, long-term storage to GEIA-STD-0003A, monthly reconciliation, annual wall-to-wall inventories, and disposal per CNSSI 3006. Logistics and warehousing only. Contemplated firm fixed price with one base year and up to eight option years. The notice asks for business size under NAICS 493190 (the NAICS field itself is blank on SAM.gov). No set-aside used.

sources.title: What is Vendor Managed Inventory (VMI)? | SAP
sources.snippet: VMI, also known as supplier-managed inventory from a customer’s point of view, is a data-driven initiative where suppliers manage the inventory levels of their own products, components, or materials at the on-site location of the vendor or distributor. This helps to reduce both shortages and surpluses. By shifting inventory management responsibilities in this way, supply chains can run leaner and more efficiently – reducing overheads and improving supply chain responsiveness and agility. [...] #

rationale.point: The opportunity's NAICS 493190 matches the company's registered NAICS code, and the work focus (inventory control, stock management, storage optimization) aligns with the company's listed capability.
The size standard for NAICS 493190 is $36.5M average annual receipts; the company is registered as small, indicating it meets this threshold.
The requirement for Vendor-Managed Inventory (VMI) services directly corresponds to the VMI definition of suppliers managing inventory levels at the customer's location.
The set-aside is NONE (unrestricted), so the company's lack of socio-economic certifications does not block eligibility per the profile's verification note.

The SAM.gov registration is still a draft with CAGE verification pending, meaning the company cannot be awarded a contract today; however, the bid due date (2026-11-30) allows time to complete registration.
The company has no past federal awards (entity started April 2026), which may weaken competitiveness given the high median top award value ($49M) in this NAICS for DoD.

risks: SAM registration and CAGE code may not be finalized before contract award.
Zero past performance record reduces evaluation credibility.
Median top award value ($49M) exceeds the NAICS size standard ($36.5M), suggesting the contract could be larger than typical small business capacity.
Company is newly formed (April 2026) with unproven operational capacity for long-term storage and VMI of microelectronics.
nextSteps: Complete SAM.gov registration and obtain CAGE code well before the award date.
Evaluate teaming with a firm that has relevant VMI/storage past performance to strengthen the proposal.
Assess the solicitation's estimated value and scope to confirm it fits within the company's capacity and the NAICS size standard.
Prepare a bid response emphasizing NAICS 493190 alignment, VMI capability per claim #3, and any relevant commercial experience.
